name: Task, Kanban, Sprint,Flows
description:
**Summary**

1. Produced `docs/planning/kanban-sprint-implementation-plan.md` (rev. 2), an implementation + migration plan for the Kanban/Sprint redesign in `codx-api`.
2. Locked in nine non-negotiable constraints (N1–N9): folder boards, files not a DB, human *oversight* rather than approval gates, zero data loss, user-defined statuses, concurrent-safe writes — plus 14 invariants (R1–R14).
3. Redefined the model: board/column folders as a projection of stable ids, a user-editable flow of statuses with bounded **categories** (`todo/active/waiting/closed`) driving all metrics, and one `TaskCard` projection shared by Kanban and Sprint.
4. Added a dedicated **concurrency** section exposing hazards in today's `store_chat`/`save_chat` (truncating writes, read-modify-write races, resurrected messages, move races) and fixing them with a single `mutate_chat` write path, locking, merge rules, tombstones and `409` conflicts.
5. Delivered a phased, zero-loss migration (P0–P5 with a journal, dry-run, review queue, rollback, gates G1–G10) decomposed into **33 independently shippable subtasks** with dependencies, acceptance criteria, sizes, API contract, risks and a test plan.

We have redundant and inconsistent design/logic between Kanban and Sprint.
We are going to redesign it:

## Task
A task that you can chat with. Can have sub tasks, can work with different projects, can define profiles, a status,...

## TaskCard
A compact way of showing important information of the task

## Kanban
A well known way to organize tasks in columns. That's it.

## Sprint
 A way to represent the flow of tasks from multiple boards focusing on their status
 
## Flows
The different status a task can be: to_do, doing, on_hold,...
User defined with some preconfigured.


----
The reason for having these boards, tasks, flows is to allow users to follow and participate in the process. Kanban and flows are the best way to quickly understand the project status. Team members (human and agents) will be updating the tasks board, status and other properties to ensure a real time a clear view of the status of the project. 

----
Right now there's a mess of concpets so we must simplified it so the rules are easy to follow for team members and we ensure a good UI/UX for human members.

----
So Kanban will be the standard to show tasks: columns with cards, sorted, with clear information and visual indication (already exists)

The "Sprint" will visualize the flow of a set of tasks. 

---

Analyze and create a pro/cons and suggest better options.

I'll analyze the existing Kanban/Sprint implementation before writing the proposal.I've mapped the current implementation. Here is the analysis document, then a summary. # Kanban & Sprint redesign — analysis, trade-offs and proposal **Status:** draft for review **Scope:** Task model, board/column storage, flows (statuses) and sprint visualisation **Code reviewed:** `codx/junior/db.py`, `codx/junior/chat_manager.py`, `codx/junior/planning_manager.py`, `codx/junior/model/planning.py`, `codx/junior/model/model.py`, `codx/junior/api/chat.py` --- ## 2. Shared vocabulary (proposed, to freeze first) Every future argument about this feature comes from the same words meaning two things. Fix the glossary before touching code. | Term | Definition | Not this | |------|-----------|----------| | **Task** | The unit of work. Has an identity, a conversation, sub-tasks, project scope, profiles, a flow status and (optionally) a placement on a board. | Not "a chat". Chat messages are *part of* a task. | | **TaskCard** | A **pure view model**: the compact projection of a task used by every board. Never persisted, never owns data. | Not a second task object. | | **Flow** | An ordered set of status definitions (`to_do`, `doing`, `on_hold`, …) with categories, colours and allowed transitions. Project-scoped, user-editable. | Not a column list. | | **Status** | The **single** flow value of a task. Owned by the task. | Not `column`. | | **Kanban (Board)** | A *placement view*: ordered columns, each holding ordered cards. Columns may **pin** a status. | Not a task container in storage. | | **Column** | A user-defined bucket inside one board, with an index, optional colour, optional pinned status and optional WIP limit. | Not a status. | | **Placement** | `board_id` + `column_id` of a task (or none = inbox). | Not a path. | | **Sprint** | A *selection + flow view*: a named set of tasks rendered through the flow stages, bounded by dates. Owns no columns. | Not a board, not a folder, not a status. | | **Activity / Status history** | Append-only events describing transitions (who, from → to, when). | Not the current value. | --- ## 3. What the code does today ### 3.1 The task is a `Chat` A "task" is a persisted `Chat` (`codx/junior/db.py`). The planning-relevant fields: | Field | Meaning today | Written by | |-------|---------------|-----------| | `board`, `column` | **Strings** used as board/column *name* **and** as filesystem directories | `save_chat`, UI metadata | | `kanban_id`, `column_id` | Ids for the same concepts — **exist but are empty everywhere** | nobody | | `status` | Free string, default `''` | planning endpoints, UI | | `status_history` | Append-only `ChatStatusEvent` log | `save_chat` → `_register_status_change` | | `sprints` | "Identifiers of the sprint **boards**" — **nothing reads it** | metadata endpoint only | | `priority`, `due_date`, `progress`, `assignees`, `sort_index` | Planning fields | planning endpoints | | `mode` | `chat` / `task` / `vibe` — used by `PlanningManager._is_task` | task generation, UI | | `project_id` / `owner_project_id` | "project the task works on" / "project that owns the file" | engine | | `parent_id`, `message_id` | Sub-tasks and threads | task generation | | `cost`, `estimation_cost` | Monotonic budget accumulation | chat manager | ### 3.2 Storage: three sources of truth for "which card is in which column" ```mermaid flowchart LR subgraph Storage F["tasks/{board}/{column}/{slug}.{id}.json"] end subgraph Metadata K["tasks/kanban.json
boards → columns → chats[] + tasks[]"] end subgraph TaskFile C["Chat.board / Chat.column
(titles as strings)"] end K -- "chats: [ids]" --> F K -- "tasks: [full chat json]" --> F C -- "path derived from titles" --> F ``` Three different keys describe the same membership: 1. `Chat.board` / `Chat.column` — **titles**, also used to build the file path (`ChatManager.get_chat_file`: `f"{chat_path}/{chat.board}/{chat.column}/{slugify(name)}.{id}.json"`). 2. `kanban.json` → `boards[key].columns[i].chats` — a list of **task ids**. 3. `kanban.json` → `boards[key].columns[i].tasks` — a list of **full copies** of the task JSON. Real inconsistencies already present in `.codx/tasks/kanban.json`: * `boards` is keyed by **title** in most cases (`"Knowledge"`, `"Bugs"`) but by **id** in others (`"Traefik"`, `"Models"`). * Board `User management` has **two columns both titled `Backlog`**, containing the same chat id. Column titles are therefore *not unique*, yet the title is used as a directory name. * Columns carry `position`, `valid`, `color`, `chats`, `tasks` — the last two are the duplicated membership. ### 3.3 Four competing board models in the codebase | Model | File | Shape | Status | |-------|------|-------|--------| | `Kanban`, `KanbanColumn` | `db.py` | TinyDB tables `kanban`, `column`, `chat`; `get_kanban_chats(kanban_id, column_id)` | second implementation, mostly unused | | `Board`, `Column` | `model/model.py` | `name`, `columns[{name, chat_ids, project_id}]`, `bookmark`, `remote_url` | third implementation, legacy | | `boards` dict | `.codx/tasks/kanban.json` | the one actually served by `GET /api/kanban` | the de-facto model | | `Chat.board` / `Chat.column` | task file | denormalised copy of the same information | the de-facto index | ### 3.4 "Status" is not a flow yet * The vocabulary is hardcoded in `planning_manager.py`: `STATUS_ORDER = ["todo", "doing", "onhold", "done", "rejected"]`. * `Chat.status` defaults to `''`, and `PlanningManager._normalize_status` silently maps unknown values to `"todo"`. * **Concrete bug produced by the redundancy:** a card dragged into a column titled `Done` keeps `status = ''` → planning reports it as `todo` → `metrics.completion` does not move, while the board shows it as finished. The opposite is equally possible: a task with `status = "done"` sitting in `Backlog`. * `status_history` records status transitions, while `planning/events.jsonl` records status/priority/assignee changes. Two event logs for one lifecycle, neither of them aware of column moves. ### 3.5 "Sprint" today is a dead field with an ambiguous definition `Chat.sprints: List[str]` describes *"the sprint boards this chat belongs to"*. No backend code reads it: no filter in `PlanningManager`, no endpoint, no projection. The only interpretation available is "a sprint is a board whose columns are sprints" — which is exactly the conflation we are trying to remove. ### 3.6 Behaviour that is a side effect of the design | Behaviour | Where | Why it hurts | |-----------|-------|--------------| | `save_chat` forces `board="kanban"`, `column="tasks"` when empty | `chat_manager.py` | Creates phantom boards/columns for anything that isn't a task | | Renaming a board or column never moves existing files | `get_chat_file` | Cards disappear from the board (path still has the old title) until each task is re-saved | | `delete_kanban(kanban_title)` does `shutil.rmtree(f"{chat_path}/{kanban_title}")` | `chat_manager.py` | A *title* is a filesystem path; a rename/typo can wipe a directory | | Sub-tasks inherit `board` **and** `column` from the parent | `chat_engine_actions.py`, `engine.py` | Generating 10 sub-tasks dumps 10 cards into the column you were focused on | | Mentions create a `mentions` board with `analysis`/`changes` columns | `mention_manager.py` | Technical logs live in the same namespace as human boards | | `_is_task()`: `mode == "chat"` without planning signal is not a task | `planning_manager.py` | The same record is a chat or a task depending on field values — the UI must guess | --- ## 4. What is good today (do not throw away) | Strength | Why it matters | |----------|----------------| | **One entity: task == chat** | The conversation, the context (`files`, `profiles`, `project_id`), the cost and the status live in one document. No issue-tracker ↔ chat sync problem. | | **Merge-safe granular message ops** | `add_message` / `update_message` / `remove_message` let agents persist tool events and streamed text mid-turn without clobbering concurrent writers. | | **Append-only `status_history`** | The raw feed for cycle time / throughput already exists and is dedup'd by `doc_id`. | | **Monotonic `Chat.cost`** | Budget survives message deletion; task cost is a first-class property. | | **Server-side aggregation** (`PlanningManager`) | Counts are computed over the whole filtered dataset, not the loaded page. | | **File-based storage** | Portable, greppable, per-project isolation, no DB to migrate, reviewable in git. | | **Free-form columns** | Real boards in this repo are *not* status boards (`Requirements`, `Tools`, `Loader`, date columns). Users need shelves, not only states. | | **Rich task payload** | `profiles`, `files`, `project_id`, `estimation_cost`, `attachments` are exactly what an agent-executable task needs. | --- ## 5. What is broken (ranked) Legend — **Impact**: how visible the problem is to a user/agent. **Fix cost**: S/M/L. | # | Problem | Evidence | Impact | Fix cost | |---|---------|----------|--------|----------| | C1 | **Presentation entangled with storage.** Board/column *titles* are directory names. | `get_chat_file()` | Rename = data loss of placement; no atomic rename exists | M | | C2 | **Triple membership.** `Chat.board/column` vs `column.chats[]` vs `column.tasks[]`. | `kanban.json` | Cards vanish / duplicate; embedded copies grow the file unboundedly | M | | C3 | **Four board models** in the codebase. | `db.py`, `model/model.py`, `kanban.json`, `Chat` | Nobody knows which is authoritative; dead code to maintain | M | | C4 | **Status ≠ column, with no mapping.** | `STATUS_ORDER` vs column titles | Board and metrics disagree; "Done" cards still count as `todo` | S | | C5 | **Keys are titles.** Board key is a title or an id; column ids exist but the tasks reference titles. | `kanban.json`, `Chat.column` | Duplicate column titles are legal, so titles cannot be keys | S | | C6 | **Sprint is undefined.** `Chat.sprints` is inert and documented as "sprint boards". | `db.py` | No way to answer "what is the flow of this set of tasks?" | M | | C7 | **No board type.** Date columns, single-column boards, scrum boards and log boards are all the same object. | `kanban.json` | The UI must guess the semantics of every board | S | | C8 | **Implicit defaults create structures.** `kanban/tasks`, `mentions/analysis`, `mentions/changes`. | `chat_manager`, `mention_manager` | Noise in the board list; boards created by machines, not people | S | | C9 | **Chat vs task is a heuristic.** | `_is_task()` | Same record, two roles, ambiguous filters ("recent chats", "tasks") | S | | C10 | **Two overlapping event logs.** `status_history` and `planning/events.jsonl`. | `chat_manager`, `planning_manager` | Metrics can be derived twice, differently | S | | C11 | **Destructive delete by title.** | `delete_kanban` | `rmtree` on a user string | S | | C12 | **No ordering contract.** `sort_index` is global; `chat_index` also exists. | `Chat` | Manual ordering in a column is not well defined | S | | C13 | **Full directory scans.** `list_chats()` reads every task file, `find_by_id()` scans all paths by substring | `chat_manager.py` | Grows with 397+ files per project; worse with embedded `tasks[]` copies | M | | C14 | **Agents have no placement rules.** Task generation copies the parent's column; nothing prevents an agent from creating boards. | `chat_engine_actions`, `engine` | Board pollution by automation | S | --- ## 6. Design options ### Option A — Harden the status quo Keep `board`/`column` as strings and as paths. Add a **mapping table** `column title → status`, make `sprints` a saved query. ```text Kanban: board (folder) → column (folder) → task files Flow: column title → status (hardcoded map in project settings) Sprint: a saved filter: board in [...] and status in [...] ``` | Pros | Cons | |------|------| | No migration, no client break | Keeps rename-as-data-loss (C1) | | Reuses 100% of current code | Membership stays ambiguous (C2, C3) | | Ships in days | Mapping by *title* breaks on rename and duplicates (C4, C5) | | | Sprint stays a second-class filter, not a first-class object | **Verdict:** acceptable as a 2-week stop-gap only. It does not remove the mess, it documents it. --- ### Option B — Decouple placement (recommended) Tasks get **ids** for placement (`board_id`, `column_id`) and a single **flow status**. Storage paths use ids only. Boards and Sprints become **views** over the same task set. ```mermaid flowchart TD T["Task (id, status, board_id, column_id, sprint_ids)"] T --> F["Flow: ordered statuses"] T --> P["Placement: board_id + column_id"] T --> S["Sprint membership"] P --> K["Kanban view: columns × cards"] F --> V["Sprint view: stages × cards"] S --> V ``` | Pros | Cons | |------|------| | Rename of board/column becomes metadata-only | Requires a one-shot migration + backfill | | One membership, one status → no drift | Needs an index file to avoid full scans | | Kanban keeps free columns (shelves) **and** can pin statuses | Two drag semantics (placement vs status) must be explained in the UI | | Sprint has no columns of its own → the Kanban/Sprint duplication disappears | Client must switch to `board_id`/`column_id` | | Reuses existing, empty `kanban_id`/`column_id` fields | | **Verdict:** best ratio between conceptual cleanliness, UX and migration cost. --- ### Option C — Flow-first (a column *is* a status) Delete the distinction: every column is a flow status. Boards become "which subset of statuses do I show". | Pros | Cons | |------|------| | Simplest possible mental model | Destroys the boards people actually use (`Requirements`, `Tools`, date columns) | | No mapping, no pinning, no second drag rule | A card can only be at one status ⇒ only one board can show it | | Sprint = filter by dates, nothing to define | Forces agile vocabulary on everyone | | Excellent for agents (one write path) | Highest migration cost for existing boards | **Verdict:** elegant, too rigid. Its useful core is kept as "columns *may* pin a status" (Option B). --- ### Option D — Generic views / query engine A "board" is a saved query: filter + group-by + sort (Jira-style). | Pros | Cons | |------|------| | No duplicated membership at all | Users must learn a query builder | | Any view becomes a configuration | Debugging "why is my card not here" becomes a query problem | | Scales to many views | Big UI investment, far from current UX | **Verdict:** the right *internal* architecture for the read path (one endpoint, many projections), wrong *user-facing* abstraction for now. --- ### Decision matrix Scores 1–5 (5 = best). | Option | Migration cost | Model simplicity | Flexibility | Rename safety | Agent-safe rules | Fit with current code | Total | |--------|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:| | A. Harden status quo | 5 | 2 | 4 | 1 | 2 | 5 | **19** | | **B. Decouple placement** | 3 | 4 | 5 | 5 | 4 | 4 | **25** | | C. Flow-first | 4 | 5 | 2 | 5 | 5 | 2 | **23** | | D. Views / query engine | 1 | 3 | 5 | 5 | 4 | 2 | **20** | --- ## 7. Recommended model (Option B, with two rules borrowed from C) ### 7.1 Entities ```mermaid classDiagram class Task { +id +name +description +status +board_id +column_id +flow_id +sprint_ids +sort_index +project_id +parent_id } class Flow class FlowStatus class Board class BoardColumn class Sprint Board "1" --> "many" BoardColumn : ordered Board --> Flow : default flow BoardColumn --> FlowStatus : optional pin Flow "1" --> "many" FlowStatus : ordered Task --> Board : placement Task --> BoardColumn : placement Task --> FlowStatus : status Sprint "1" --> "many" Task : membership Task --> Task : sub tasks ``` Sketch (fields only — no behaviour change to the existing `Chat`): ```python class FlowStatus(BaseModel): key: str # "doing" label: str # "Doing" category: str # "todo" | "active" | "waiting" | "closed" color: str = "" index: int = 0 wip_limit: Optional[int] = None allowed_from: Optional[List[str]] = None # None = any predecessor class Flow(BaseModel): id: str name: str statuses: List[FlowStatus] default_status: str = "todo" class BoardColumn(BaseModel): id: str title: str # free text, editable, NOT a path index: int color: Optional[str] = None status_key: Optional[str] = None # pin: dropping a card here sets FlowStatus wip_limit: Optional[int] = None class Board(BaseModel): id: str name: str columns: List[BoardColumn] flow_id: Optional[str] = None parent_id: Optional[str] = None kind: str = "kanban" # "kanban" | "log" (hidden from the board list) class Sprint(BaseModel): id: str name: str start_date: Optional[str] = None end_date: Optional[str] = None goal: str = "" flow_id: str board_ids: List[str] = [] # contributing boards (optional filter) task_ids: List[str] = [] # explicit membership include_statuses: List[str] = [] # optional filter, e.g. hide closed class Task(Chat): # extend the existing model, do not fork it board_id: str = "" column_id: str = "" flow_id: str = "" sprint_ids: List[str] = [] ``` `Chat.board` / `Chat.column` (titles) become **derived, read-only projections** filled on serialisation. ### 7.2 Invariants (the part that makes the rules easy to follow) | # | Rule | Enforced by | |---|------|-------------| | R1 | A task has exactly **one** placement (`board_id` + `column_id`) or none → inbox. | board API validation | | R2 | A task has exactly **one** status, always valid in its flow. | transition endpoint | | R3 | Task files are stored as `tasks/{board_id}/{task_id}.json` — **the column is never in the path**. | `get_chat_file` | | R4 | Renaming a board/column/sprint is metadata-only: no file moves. | R3 | | R5 | A column **with** `status_key` mirrors a status: moving a card sets `status`. A column **without** it is a shelf: moving a card changes placement only. | drag handler | | R6 | Sprint membership never changes placement nor status. | sprint API | | R7 | Sprint has no columns: its stages are the flow stages (ordered by `FlowStatus.index`). | read model | | R8 | Ordering: `sort_index` is unique per `(board_id, column_id)`. Sprint ordering = `(status index, sort_index)`. | reorder endpoint | | R9 | Status changes are appended to `status_history` (`from`, `to`, `user`, `at`) — single source for metrics. `events.jsonl` keeps *field* changes, not status. | `save_chat` | | R10 | Agents may: create tasks in the inbox, move them within a board, set a status through an allowed transition. Agents may **not** create/rename/delete boards, flows or sprints. | authorisation layer | | R11 | Deleting a board moves its tasks to the inbox; deleting tasks requires an explicit flag. Never `rmtree` a user string. | board API | | R12 | Only one writer per field: placement via the board API, status via the transition API. | API surface | ### 7.3 Storage layout ```text # today .codx/tasks/ kanban.json # boards + columns + chats[] + tasks[] (duplicated) Knowledge/To Do/task-a..json Knowledge/Done/task-b..json # proposed .codx/planning/ flows.json # project flows (seeded default) boards.json # board ids → columns (ordered, pins, wip) sprints.json # sprint definitions + membership index.json # task_id → board_id (avoids full scans) events.jsonl # field-level activity .codx/tasks/ /.json # task document is the only source of truth inbox/.json ``` Example task document (excerpt): ```json { "id": "6f0c…", "name": "Redesign sprint view", "status": "doing", "flow_id": "default", "board_id": "engine", "column_id": "in-development", "sprint_ids": ["sprint-2026-04"], "sort_index": 3, "priority": "high", "assignees": ["ana"], "profiles": ["software_developer"], "project_id": "ac9804d5", "parent_id": null } ``` ### 7.4 API surface | Endpoint | Purpose | |----------|---------| | `GET /api/flows`, `PUT /api/flows/{id}` | Read/write flows and statuses | | `GET /api/boards`, `POST /api/boards`, `PATCH /api/boards/{id}` | Board CRUD (rename = metadata) | | `GET /api/boards/{id}/cards?assignee=&priority=&q=` | Kanban read model (columns + cards) | | `PATCH /api/tasks/{id}/placement` | Move a card (sets status if the column is pinned) | | `PATCH /api/tasks/{id}/status` | Transition (guarded by flow) | | `POST /api/tasks/{id}/reorder` | `sort_index` inside a column | | `GET /api/sprints`, `POST /api/sprints`, `PATCH /api/sprints/{id}` | Sprint definition | | `GET /api/sprints/{id}/flow` | Sprint read model: stages × cards + metrics | | `POST /api/sprints/{id}/tasks` | Add/remove membership (bulk) | Both read models return the **same card projection object**, so `TaskCard` is defined once. ### 7.5 TaskCard — the compact card Content contract (max 6 elements, fixed order, no vertical growth): ```text ┌─────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ ▸ Redesign the sprint view ● doing │ title (2 lines max) + status chip │ #4 · high · due in 2d │ key badges: subtasks, priority, due │ ████████░░░░ 60% │ progress (only when 0 < p < 100) │ 👤 ana 👤 bot-dev ⌛ 3d stale │ assignees (max 3) + staleness └─────────────────────────────────────────┘ ``` Rules: * The card never renders the description, the transcript, or tool output. * Colour comes from `FlowStatus.color` — one colour vocabulary for Kanban and Sprint. * Overdue / needs-attention is a single icon driven by server-computed flags (`overdue`, `due_today`, `unassigned`, `stalled` — already produced by `PlanningManager`). * Unread messages from others (existing `read_by`) render as a dot, not a number, to avoid noise. ### 7.6 Kanban UX rules * Columns are ordered, scroll vertically per column, horizontal scroll for the board. The column header shows `count` and, if set, `count / wip_limit`. * Default sort: manual (`sort_index`). Optional overrides: priority, due date. * Drag inside a column = reorder. Drag across columns = placement (+ status when the target column is pinned — the card flashes the new status chip so the rule is learned instantly). * A board may be created from a template: `Status board` (columns pinned to the flow), `Shelf board` (free columns), `Log board` (`kind="log"`, hidden from the picker, used by mentions/automation). * Empty columns are collapsed to a narrow strip, never removed automatically. ### 7.7 Sprint UX rules * Header: name, dates, goal, `done / total`, `% complete`, `blocked`, `unassigned`. * Body: one lane per flow stage, left→right in flow order. No customisation (that's the point — it is a *flow*). * Drag a card between lanes = **status change only**. Board placement is untouched; if the card's column pins that status, its Kanban position follows automatically (R5). * Cards not placed on any board appear here too (a sprint is a selection, not a placement). * Bulk action: "move all `doing` to `on_hold`" for end-of-day triage. ### 7.8 Walkthrough — one task, both views | Step | Kanban (board `engine`) | Sprint (`2026-04`) | Task fields touched | |------|------------------------|--------------------|---------------------| | 1 | Card created in `Inbox` | not in sprint | `board_id=inbox`, `status=to_do` | | 2 | Dragged to `Backlog` (shelf) | not in sprint | placement only | | 3 | Added to sprint | appears in `To do` lane | `sprint_ids += [2026-04]` | | 4 | Dragged to `Doing` lane in Sprint | `Doing` lane | `status=doing` | | 5 | Card is now in `In Development` (pinned to `doing`) | `Doing` lane | placement updated by the pin | | 6 | Agent finishes, sets `done` | `Done` lane, counters move | `status=done` + `status_history` | --- ## 8. Migration plan | Phase | Deliverable | Acceptance criteria | |-------|-------------|---------------------| | **P0** Vocabulary | This document + `Flow` model + seeded default flow (`to_do, doing, on_hold, done, rejected` with categories) | `GET /api/flows` returns the default; no data changed | | **P1** Ids | Backfill `kanban_id`/`column_id` from `kanban.json`; assign `column.status_key` where the column title matches a flow label | Every task has ids; report of tasks whose titles and ids disagreed | | **P2** New paths | Write `tasks/{board_id}/{task_id}.json`, dual-read legacy paths; add `planning/index.json` | Round-trip on a copy of `.codx/tasks` (397 files, 152 folders) with zero card lost | | **P3** Read models | `/api/boards/{id}/cards` and `/api/sprints/{id}/flow`; both return the same card projection | Kanban and Sprint can be built without any legacy endpoint | | **P4** UI cut-over | Feature flag per view | Same cards, same counts on both views; drag semantics match R5/R6 | | **P5** Removal | Drop `kanban.json` writes, TinyDB `kanban`/`column` tables, `Board`/`Column` in `model/model.py`, `Chat.board/column` as inputs, `DEFAULT_BOARD`/`DEFAULT_COLUMN`, `Chat.sprints` | `grep` for the legacy names returns only the migration notes | Backfill algorithm (P1), in one paragraph: read `kanban.json`; for each board key, resolve `id` (existing `id` field, else generate and log); for each column, take `id`; build the set `chats ∪ tasks[].id`; for each task id set `board_id`/`column_id`. When a task appears in two columns, prefer the column whose title matches the task's current `column` string; if there is still ambiguity, keep the first by column `position` and emit a warning row so a human can arbitrate. Finally verify every `board_id`/`column_id` referenced exists. ### Risks | Risk | Mitigation | |------|-----------| | A board rename still leaves files in the old folder during the transition | P2 writes by id; legacy files are re-saved on first mutation; a one-shot mover script closes the gap | | Duplicate columns/boards (see `Backlog` twice) collapse into one id | Report + human arbitration before deletion, never auto-merge | | Tasks with no board | First-class `inbox` board, never `board=""` | | Performance regression | `planning/index.json` + per-board `board.json`; `find_by_id` stops scanning paths | | Users attached to free columns | Keep shelves; pin only where the title matches a flow label, and show a one-time "this column now mirrors *Doing*" notice | | Two drag rules confuse people | Card always flashes the status chip it just acquired; Sprint shows the rule explicitly ("status only") | --- ## 9. Concurrent write safety (N9 — must land before anything else) Every task file has several potential writers *at the same time*: the AI engine (holds a chat in memory for the whole turn and calls `save_chat` repeatedly), the human UI (`PUT /api/chats`, `PATCH /api/planning/tasks/{id}`), agent tools, sub-task generation, mentions, and the migration CLI. ### 4.1 Hazards found in the current code | # | Hazard | Where | Effect | |---|---|---|---| | H1 | **Non-atomic write** — `open(path, "w")` truncates before writing | `ChatManager.store_chat`, `save_kanban` | Crash / full disk / OOM → zero-length or truncated JSON → `list_chats` logs and **skips the file** → the task silently disappears from every board | | H2 | **Read-modify-write race** — `current_chat = self.find_by_id(...)` … `store_chat(...)` with no lock; the read scans the whole tree (`rglob`) so the window is wide | `save_chat` | Last writer wins for **every** field, including `messages` | | H3 | **`chat_only=True` preserves only messages** | `save_chat` | `status`, `priority`, `due_date`, `assignees`, `progress`, `status_history`, `cost`, `file_list` are taken from possibly stale memory → `PlanningManager.update_task` overwrites a concurrent status change | | H4 | **No tombstones** — `_merge_message_lists` merges by `doc_id` only | `chat_manager.py` | A stale `save_chat` **resurrects a removed message** and drops messages added elsewhere | | H5 | **Engine writes from memory** | `Engine.save_chat`, `chat_engine_actions`, socket handlers | The AI loop persists its in-memory chat mid-run; a human edit in that window is lost | | H6 | **File-move race** | `save_chat` → `delete_chat(current_chat.file_path)` | Two writers computing different `file_path` (rename in flight) can delete each other's fresh file | | H7 | **Socket event without revision** | `EventManager.chat_event` sends `{id, text, type}` only | Clients refetch and can apply an older snapshot than the one on disk | | ✔ | **Already correct — copy this pattern** | `status_history` (append-only, dedup by `doc_id`), `cost` (monotonic `max`), `_accumulate_message_cost`, `PlanningManager.update_task`'s `expected_updated_at` | Merge-safe, monotonic, conflict-detecting | ### 4.2 The single write path ```text mutate_chat(chat_id, mutator, *, expected_updated_at=None, actor, actor_type) └─ with chat_lock(chat_id): # in-process + fcntl flock on .lock stored = load_fresh(chat_id) # index.json fast path, then rglob if expected_updated_at and stored.updated_at != expected_updated_at: raise PlanningConflictError(fresh=stored) # 409, never a silent overwrite base = copy(stored) mutator(base) # mutator ALWAYS receives fresh state base = merge(base, stored) # see table below base.updated_at = now(); base.revision = (stored.revision or 0) + 1 base.updated_by, base.updated_by_type = actor, actor_type atomic_write(base, path=path_from_ids(base)) # tmp + fsync + os.replace emit("chat-event", {id, revision, updated_at}) # clients can discard stale payloads return base ``` Rules: **never hold the lock across an AI call** (short critical sections only); lock ordering is always *chat lock → index lock* (never the reverse); `store_chat()` becomes private to `mutate_chat`. ### 4.3 Field merge strategies (what wins) | Field | Strategy on merge | |---|---| | `messages` | Merge by `doc_id`, last `updated_at` wins, **minus `deleted_message_ids` tombstones**. Never wholesale replace. | | `deleted_message_ids` | Union of tombstones (append-only, capped at 500 with `deleted_at`-ordered eviction). | | `status_history` | Union by `doc_id`, sorted by `at` (already implemented). | | `cost` | `max(stored, incoming)` — monotonic (already implemented). | | `revision`, `updated_at` | Always bumped by the writer; never taken from the caller. | | `status`, `priority`, `due_date`, `assignees`, `progress`, `sort_index` | **Field-owned**: only via the dedicated endpoint, guarded by `expected_updated_at` → `409 Conflict` with the fresh task in the body. | | `board_id`, `column_id`, `board`, `column` | **Placement-owned**: only `move_task`/rename; `save_chat` never touches them (`touch_placement=False`). | | `name` | **Rename-owned**: only the rename path (it changes the file name). | | `users`, `profiles` | Union. | | `file_list`, `attachments`, `tags` | Union, dedup (avoids losing a reference added by another writer). | | `messages[].read_by` | Union per message (`mark_message_as_seen` already goes through `update_message`). | | everything else | Last writer wins, with attribution recorded. | ### 4.4 Agent ↔ human interaction during a run * An agent tool call never writes a snapshot it read minutes ago: it calls the same endpoint a human would, so the lock + merge applies. * On `409` the tool wrapper re-reads **once** and re-applies against fresh state (e.g. "set status=done" survives a concurrent priority change); a second conflict is reported back into the chat as a visible tool event, not retried blindly. * A human editing a card while an agent works on it is **always allowed** — that is N1. The agent sees the new state and the history shows both actors. * Interruption uses the existing `CANCELLATION_REGISTRY` (`POST /api/chat/cancel` by `chat_id` or `token_id`); stopping a run leaves all partial work persisted (mid-run writes are already merge-safe). ### 4.5 Concurrency tests (gate G9) 1. Two threads: `add_message(A)` vs `set_status(B)` with a 200 ms sleep in between → both survive. 2. `remove_message(X)` then a stale `save_chat(chat_with_X)` → X stays deleted (tombstone). 3. Two writers with different `file_path` (rename vs edit) → exactly one file, no orphan. 4. Injected `OSError` on `os.replace` → original file intact, `.tmp` cleaned up. 5. Kill -9 during a write → file parses or the previous version is intact (never truncated). 6. `expected_updated_at` mismatch → `409` + fresh task, no write. --- ## 5.
